meta.title: Predicted spawning
meta.subtitle: Two independent streams, one matcher, and an entity that is adopted rather than replaced

views.label: The client half
views.note: The entity exists in the same frame as the input. Ghost id zero marks it as unadopted.

views.label: The matcher
views.note: Same ghost type, spawn ticks within a window. Nothing else is compared by default.

views.label: Adopt or reap
views.note: A hit keeps the client entity. A miss leaves it in the list until the interpolation tick passes.

cards.title: Why the client spawns at all
items: A projectile cannot be predicted before it exists
Waiting for the server puts a full round trip where attention is highest
So the client creates it, and the server's ghost takes over that same entity
The adopted entity keeps its transform, its trail, and every local component

cards.title: Why the match is a window
items: Inside prediction the client stamps the tick it is simulating
Outside prediction it stamps the last full server tick
The server stamps its own tick at the end of its frame
Spawning inside the prediction loop is the single best accuracy fix

cards.title: The two failures look nothing alike
items: No match: two projectiles briefly, then the client copy is destroyed
Wrong match: one projectile adopts another's ghost and snaps to it
Widening the window converts misses into mismatches
Narrowing it converts mismatches back into misses

cards.title: When to write your own matcher
items: As soon as two ghosts of one type can spawn within the window
Shotguns, burst fire, swarms, anything with a fast rate of fire
Match on a replicated sequence number written identically on both sides
An exact key removes the window and both failure modes with it
